samples.marker_line: npm test fixture: injection regression case; retain hook detections
evidence: All 130 bytes match testdata/triage/vscode-version-drift/consumer-injection/package.json; fixture identity is independently corroborated by the repository cases.json and positive-fixture documentation.

npm runs the preinstall shell from the package directory. cd ../../.. crosses out of it; && invokes npm install injected-package only after successful navigation. This can modify a consumer manifest/lockfile and run dependency hooks.
No obfuscation or other executable content exists in the sample. The name fixture is corroboration, not the basis for suppressing behavior. Preserve the accurate injection/hook observations.
No registry provenance or real deployment was supplied. Fixture byte identity tips the verdict; a copy deployed as an unexpected dependency would need its deployment context investigated.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Verified benign regression fixture remains classified HOSTILE; preserve accurate behavioral observations and report the model/provenance gap.

samples.marker_line: DarkCore builder: secret theft and clipboard address hijacking
evidence: CLR entry token 0x0600002b resolves to MyApplication.Main; OnCreateMainForm constructs the controller UI. SenderBuilder.Build reads client source resources, including CryptoClipperHook.vb, and includes them in generated client builds. This artifact is a controller/builder, not an already-configured victim stub.

Fully decoded .resources serialized strings using ECMA/.NET 7-bit lengths (the library initially truncated multi-byte lengths). Traced clipboard RegisterConsumer to OnHubClipboardEvent, OnClipboardChanged, per-currency regex matching, address-map lookup, replacement assignment, and ClipboardHub.TrySetText. Addresses are build-time placeholders or operator updates.

CommandReceiver exposes enable/disable/update operations for the clipper. Keylogging, browser/Discord/wallet collection, Telegram reporting, hidden desktop control, and Phone Link phone.db copying and SMS serialization are present in client templates.

Managed IL analysis of AssemblyProtector.EncryptStrings and related methods shows a builder that rewrites IL and adds obfuscation/protection. API-name co-occurrence and large resources do not prove that this controller starts by decrypting and launching a resource.

The native browser helper at 0x5daf53 duplicates browser-owned file handles, copies a target database into a temporary file, and extracts browser key material. CopyFileA at VA 0x1800080d7 is a fallback when the browser file handle is unavailable, not a self-copy. SetFilePointer resets the source handle for copying.

The helper IsDebuggerPresent import is called at VA 0x180008a3f in the CRT fatal-error/exception-reporting routine, followed by exception-filter setup. It is not a debugger gate on an embedded payload.

Credential theft plus unattended cryptocurrency-address replacement and concealed client operation establish hostile purpose. No operator authorization or actual victim deployment was supplied; the builder role does not erase these implemented attack capabilities.

samples.identification: WinRAR SFX carrying Xeno and UPX-packed Salat RAT
samples.marker_line: Xeno SFX: silently launches Salat credential stealer and RAT
evidence: RAR5 overlay starts at offset 449024. The SFX comment sets Path=%temp%, two Setup executables (Xeno=v1.3.65.exe and Xeno-v1.3.65.exe), Silent=1, Overwrite=1 and Update=U. Both executable members are therefore launch targets, including the separate stealer.

Extracted the stored 3,586,048-byte sidecar. UPX unpacked it to 12,570,112 bytes. Disassembled recovered Go functions and call sites; the Salat family markers corroborate the program identity but do not substitute for the following behavior.

main.doTask dispatches received tasks to process execution, downloadFile, shell execution, screenshot collection, Steal and p2pSocks. main.runKeylogger opens a recording file, installs hooks and records input.

main.getChromeLogins queries login stores and calls DecryptChrome; GetChromiumMasterKeys reads Local State and uses base64/DPAPI/app-bound decryption. main.Steal enumerates browser, Discord, Steam and wallet sources, creates a ZIP, encodes/serializes it, and calls dec then rq for submission. sendScreen likewise captures, encodes, serializes and submits screen contents.

main.staticinstall directly calls main.newTask and registry.Key.setStringValue with a CurrentVersion\Run path. main.newTask calls taskmaster CreateTask. main.Suicide deletes registered tasks and staged files. These are verified execution paths, not conclusions drawn from symbol names alone.

The bundled Xeno.dll implements game-process memory/injection functionality. Its ep.zst.enc URL is an encrypted application download, not a victim filename or a ransom demand. Its remote-memory API profile remains suspicious; the unrelated ransom classification is removed.

Silent launch of the credential-stealing RAT alongside the installer tips the verdict. No evidence identifies the distributor or proves that the other installer is an authentic upstream release. Neither uncertainty is necessary to establish the hostile sidecar behavior.

corrections.correction: Preserve module-path/copy/read/write/seek APIs as neutral handle-I/O profiles. Browser database copying is a concrete counterexample; no source/destination or image mutation relationship is required by the old rules.
Retain unsigned/header-walk/DOS-bytes/debugger-import profile as notable PE parsing. Trace the only IsDebuggerPresent call to CRT error reporting; no loader gate is established.
Keep the service-name/suspended-memory API profile suspicious. Neither target binding nor a privilege transition is required by its matcher.
Keep registry hive/write/RNG co-occurrence notable. RNG use elsewhere in a builder cannot establish randomized registry writes.

Keep resource/codec/decrypt/activation API profiles notable in capability homes. The old matchers do not bind a resource to decryption, module loading or execution; this controller uses resources for source templates and bundled tools.
Keep game references plus remote-memory APIs suspicious, with neutral game filename observations. Static API co-occurrence does not establish the target data flow or hostile use.

limitations: No sample was executed. Static paths establish supported capabilities but do not prove successful infection or collection on a victim.
The provided sandbox URLs were unavailable; no sandbox-only claims were converted into static detections.
